original.title: Exchange and Power in Social Life
original.note: Classic book with no clean OpenAlex/Crossref record (searches return reviews or reprints). Check by ISBN before publishing; shown with a ? chip until then.

core_idea: Social relationships can be understood as exchanges of rewards and costs, material or not (help, approval, status, information). Exchanges are governed by norms such as reciprocity; they build trust and obligation over time, and unequal dependence in an exchange creates power.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Why do employees go beyond their role, stay or leave (in response to support, fairness, trust)?
How do reciprocity and dependence shape relationships in families, communities or organizations?
Typical data: surveys (perceived support, trust, commitment), interviews on give-and-take in relationships.
common_mistakes: Using 'social exchange' as a general label for any relationship without specifying what is exchanged and under which rules.
Explaining outcomes after the fact without predicting anything in advance.
Ignoring power and dependence, which are central to the theory.

development.adds: Social behaviour as an exchange of material and non-material goods.

work.title: The Norm of Reciprocity: A Preliminary Statement

development.adds: The norm of reciprocity as a near-universal rule that stabilizes exchange.
